answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a fixed deposit before it may post offers, then slash that deposit when a randomly selected, independently verified counterparty proves a signed interaction was fabricated. Splitting one operator across a hundred identities does not multiply influence for free: each identity ties up capital, and each caught lie destroys a deposit. A quill-sized stake on a knoll of accounts still leaves a hollow strategy if expected slashing exceeds the value of manipulation.
